question: The Supreme Court judgment that decriminalised consensual sexual conduct between adults of the same sex in India was:

answers.text: Lillu alias Rajesh v State of Haryana (2013) — which held that two-finger tests on rape survivors are unconstitutional.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Lillu (2013) addressed the unconstitutionality of the two-finger (vaginal laxity) test in rape examinations, not decriminalisation of same-sex conduct. It is a different landmark ruling with direct relevance to rape examination practice.

answers.text: Navtej Singh Johar v Union of India (2018) — which struck down Section 377 of the IPC to the extent it criminalised consensual adult same-sex conduct.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Navtej Singh Johar v UOI (2018) held that Section 377 IPC, in so far as it criminalised consensual sexual conduct between competent adults, was unconstitutional. Non-consensual and acts involving minors remain criminal. The judgment established that sexual orientation is a protected attribute of identity.

answers.text: Joseph Shine v Union of India (2018) — which decriminalised adultery and same-sex conduct simultaneously.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Joseph Shine v UOI (2018) struck down IPC Section 497 (adultery) as unconstitutional — a separate matter involving heterosexual adultery law, not same-sex conduct. Both judgments were delivered in 2018 but address distinct issues.

answers.text: Shafin Jahan v Asokan (2018) — which upheld the right to choose a marriage partner of any gender.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Shafin Jahan (2018) concerned the right to choose a spouse in an interfaith marriage (the 'Love Jihad' case) — it did not address same-sex conduct or Section 377.

overallFeedback.feedback: Navtej Singh Johar v Union of India (2018) struck down Section 377 IPC for consensual adult same-sex acts. Lillu (2013) = two-finger test unconstitutional. Joseph Shine (2018) = adultery decriminalised. Know these three judgments separately.

Correct. Navtej Singh Johar (2018) is the landmark ruling. As a clinician, you must not treat consensual adult same-sex conduct as criminal, and examining doctors must not produce MLCs that pathologise sexual orientation.
